extracted.intended_audience: educational institution administrators, Title IX coordinators/compliance officers, legal counsel, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and implementation guidance from the Department of Education's final Title IX regulations concerning discrimination based on pregnancy or related conditions (including termination of pregnancy), parental status, admissions-related inquiries, and related institutional obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on inquiries into abortion circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient can implement these regulations without asking questions of a student, employee, or applicant for admission or employment about the specific circumstances surrounding the person's pregnancy or related conditions, including a potential or past abortion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inquiries into the circumstances of an abortion may be discriminatory—for example, if informed by sex stereotypes or handled differently than inquiries into other temporary medical conditions—or may impermissibly deter a student or employee from exercising Title IX rights. Recipients should avoid asking such questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 1688 abortion-neutrality limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in Title IX or these final regulations requires recipients to provide or pay for benefits or services, including the use of facilities, related to an abortion (20 U.S.C. 1688).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations are consistent with 20 U.S.C. 1688 and do not require recipients to pay for or provide abortion services or coverage. Section 1688 provides a partial limitation on Department enforcement regarding abortion-related benefits but does not require exempting abortion from the definition of 'pregnancy or related conditions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of 'termination of pregnancy' in 'pregnancy or related conditions'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department interprets the terms 'pregnancy or related conditions' and 'termination of pregnancy' to include termination of pregnancy; Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization does not alter this interpretation or the Department's nondiscrimination mandate under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department is not adopting the final regulations as a response to Dobbs. The inclusion is intended to ensure nondiscrimination for individuals who seek or have had abortions and to clarify recipient obligations at all stages of pregnancy, including through recovery and related medical conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department authority to regulate pregnancy-related discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department has statutory authority under Title IX and Congress' express delegation (20 U.S.C. 1682) to issue regulations prohibiting sex discrimination, including discrimination based on pregnancy or related conditions, such as termination of pregnancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition on discrimination based on termination of pregnancy has been present in Title IX regulations since 1975; the Department's regulation of such discrimination does not raise concerns under the major questions doctrine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking reasonableness and cost-benefit rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Defining 'pregnancy or related conditions' to include termination of pregnancy is not arbitrary and capricious; the Department explained costs and benefits in the Regulatory Impact Analysis and considered public comment and stakeholder engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department is not required to cite statistics for every underlying issue when conducting rulemaking. The inclusion is a considered judgment about how best to effectuate Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide reasonable modifications for students (but not employees)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must make reasonable modifications for students that are necessary to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access to the recipient's education program or activity, based on the student's individualized needs in consultation with the student. A recipient is not required to provide reasonable modifications for employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such reasonable modifications will be determined case-by-case and typically are not expected to be particularly expensive or extensive; they apply at all stages of pregnancy including recovery and related medical conditions (see final §106.40(b)(3)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of lactation space for students and employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations contain provisions requiring lactation space for students and employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lactation-space requirements are part of the pregnancy-related protections and are meant to promote continued access to education and employment; these provisions do not encourage or discourage pregnancy or termination of pregnancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination-of-pregnancy discrimination is sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination based on termination of pregnancy is sex discrimination because pregnancy discrimination has long been recognized as an aspect of sex discrimination, because pregnancy is a sex-characteristic, and because such discrimination can operate via sex stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law and the 1975 Title IX regulations support treating pregnancy (including termination) discrimination as sex discrimination; discrimination can be based on stereotypes or sex-based indifference to needs of pregnant persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with other Federal laws and independent authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX's protections for pregnancy or related conditions do not require recipients to pay for abortions and are consistent with other Federal laws. Section 1557 and Title IX are independent authorities; if a program is subject to both, the recipient must comply with both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns that Title IX would force recipients to cover abortions in health insurance are mistaken. The Department will not alter obligations under other statutes; overlapping obligations should be managed without assuming Title IX supersedes them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of alternative approaches as substitutes for regulatory coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department considered alternatives (e.g., adoption assistance, free medical care, separate rulemaking) but believes coverage of termination of pregnancy within 'pregnancy or related conditions' is necessary to prevent sex discrimination; some commenter-suggested measures (lactation spaces, reasonable modifications) are already included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other suggestions may be beyond the scope of these final regulations, but the Department will offer technical assistance and guidance as appropriate to promote compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Amendment and religious freedom safeguards preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: The pregnancy-related provisions do not limit protections for free exercise of religion, free speech, or other constitutional rights; the regulations do not change the existing religious exemption for recipients controlled by religious organizations (20 U.S.C. 1681(a)(3) and §106.12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients cannot use Title IX to limit protected religious expression. The Department reaffirms commitment to being consistent with the First Amendment and federal religious freedom statutes (e.g., RFRA). The Department posts correspondence regarding religious exemptions for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'parental status' and scope of protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department defines 'parental status' in §106.2 to include categories such as in loco parentis, legal custodian or guardian, and actively seeking legal custody/guardianship/visitation/adoption, to clarify Title IX's prohibition on sex discrimination related to parental status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition does not bestow parental authority or alter state-determined parental rights; determinations about who fits categories such as 'in loco parentis' or 'legal custodian or guardian' depend on facts and state law. The Department declined to add specific examples and declined to add a separate category for domestic partners or parents via assisted reproductive technology because many categories already encompass those situations depending on facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age threshold for 'parental status' coverage remains 18
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to raise the age of the person receiving care from 18 to 21; the definition includes persons over 18 who are incapable of self-care because of a physical or mental disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most States set the age of legal majority at 18; parental status protections are aligned with that norm and do not alter parental rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions protections and scope (Section 106.21(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.21(c) prohibits discrimination against applicants for admission based on parental, family, or marital status and pregnancy or related conditions, ensuring these statuses do not affect admission chances and supporting inclusive educational access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised wording for clarity (e.g., 'implement' for 'apply', 'adopt or implement' for 'establish or follow') and confirms Subpart C admissions provisions do not apply to nonvocational elementary and secondary schools; §106.34 addresses nonvocational elementary/secondary school participation and single-sex public schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-admission inquiry restrictions and 'all applicants' rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients covered by Subpart C must not implement policies, practices, or procedures—including pre-admission inquiries—concerning parental, family, or marital status that treat applicants differently based on sex. A pre-admission question is permissible only if asked of all applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to separately add 'current, potential, or past pregnancy or related conditions' to the pre-admission inquiry prohibition because §106.21(c)(2)(i) and (ii) already prohibit discrimination based on those statuses; the Common Application's parental-status question was noted as a research data source. The Department also replaced phrasing 'such applicants of both sexes' with 'all applicants' for inclusivity and grammatical clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declination to add 'perceived' and 'expected' as protected modifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to add 'perceived' and 'expected' to the list of protected statuses in §106.21(c)(2)(ii) (and similarly in the definition of pregnancy), rejecting the commenters' suggestion to explicitly include these modifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department's rationale for this decline is explained in the discussion of §106.10; existing provisions and doctrines (e.g., sex-stereotype and proxy discrimination theories) capture many harms related to perception-based discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality protections for personally identifiable information (PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(j) was revised to prohibit the disclosure of personally identifiable information obtained in the course of complying with Part 106, with certain exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change addresses commenter concerns about maintaining confidentiality of PII collected through compliance activities (e.g., admissions processes and accommodations). Recipients must follow §106.44(j) confidentiality limits while complying with Title IX obligations.
